name: GazeIntent
summary: Gaze-only dwell selection whose dwell time shrinks when a machine-learning model, reading your eye movements, predicts that you are about to select.
howItWorks: An LSTM intent model reads 17-sample windows of gaze velocity, displacement and acceleration (plus fixation and saccade flags) and predicts whether the user intends to select. The last four predictions are combined into a scaling factor that cuts the static dwell threshold, down to instant selection when the model is confident, so false positives from single predictions are damped. The model (F1 = 0.94) was trained on controller selections in an arithmetic task on a Meta Quest Pro, then deployed for gaze-only selection in a Fitts-style task, arithmetic grids and a sliding puzzle. Compared with static dwell and a dwell-then-intent method (after Isomoto et al.), GazeIntent allowed many more selections in the faster tasks, felt fastest, and personalised models were preferred by most returning users.

relationships.note: Adapts the dwell threshold with a real-time intent model.
